scope: Decide only the first governed syllable-structure policy and treatment of adjacent vowel phonemes. Do not decide diphthong inventory, glide formation, lexical stress, whole-word pronunciation, romanization redesign, DAYI semantics or curriculum.

analysis: The language cannot adopt a blanket rule that adjacent vowels are forbidden, because FROZEN lexical material contains them under the affirmed G40=/y/ analysis.
The corpus supports allowing adjacent vowel phonemes, but does not yet determine whether each sequence is hiatus, diphthong or subject to glide formation.
A conservative first policy can govern permissible phoneme sequencing without prematurely fixing syllable boundaries or pronunciation.

options.description: Affirm that HNK lexical forms may contain adjacent vowel phonemes, including VVV sequences. Treat exact syllable boundaries, hiatus/diphthong status and glide formation as unresolved until B3/B4. Retire the blanket authoring preference 'avoid hiatus' as a canonical-language assumption, while preserving it as historical prior.
options.effect: Preserves FROZEN Y-bearing forms without inventing word-level pronunciation; permits B3 to test diphthong/glide behavior.

options.description: Treat every adjacent vowel phoneme as a separate syllabic nucleus unless a later exception is explicitly governed.
options.effect: Creates a stronger syllabification rule now, including provisional multi-syllabic readings for DAYI and other Y-bearing forms.

options.description: Do not govern adjacent vowels yet; open a broader syllable-system design investigation before allowing B3.
options.effect: Blocks B3-B6 and leaves the old phonotactic conflict unresolved.
